allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of saguaro growth at sites like Saguaro National Park: about a metre by 40 years, a few metres by 80, about seven by 125. Wide tolerances; replace with measured growth curves before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: a dull grey-green skin with darker pleats, 12 to 24 ribs by girth, areoles about 2.5 cm apart with brown felt, a dozen or more short radial spines and a few longer, darker centrals, the lowest pointing down, greying with age; old plants corky at the base. Waxy white flowers with yellow centres.

appearance.bodies.stem.areoles.spacing.note: Spec rework E6c: the cacti's ribs, areoles and spines grown from the characters their floras state, in each body look that has ribs or a spine set of that role.

appearance.organs.flower.shape.note: Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5): tepals on a spiral, from green outer ones to waxy white inner ones, on a floral tube and an inferior ovary, from the characters of Cactaceae by the rules at the flowering plants. By hand (as search results quote them; the pages themselves were not read): 24 tepals (no count found); the pericarpel and floral tube, 6 to 10 cm of a flower 8.5 to 12.5 cm long, as 1.2 of the flower's radius; 200 stamens, the most a flower draws, for the thousands floras count.

appearance.organs.flower.shape.corolla.note: How PlantGen draws a flower, a choice of the model's (spec rework P5): the flower characters set a flower card's perianth, its parts, how they differ by place, how far the corolla is joined into a tube, a floral cup, where the ovary sits, a resupinate flower's turn, its stamens, staminodes and carpels and its spurs. The rules also set these fields in a season's flower and bud looks that draw a flower, unless set there by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a single ribbed column that grows a few centimetres in its first decade and fastest in middle age, to 12 to 15 m in about two centuries; its tip widens to an adult diameter near 50 cm, so juveniles are club-shaped. Arms come late (after about 65 years and 3 m), from the middle of the trunk, nearly level, turning up at a constricted elbow; a few droop after freezes. White flowers ring the tips of trunk and arms in late spring with buds and red fruit. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.dioecious.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant bears both sexes, unless its taxa state it dioecious.

generator.params.radius_max.note: Spec rework E6c: a column's or barrel's girth from its stated diameter.

generator.params.sex.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant's sex is its own draw, dealt across a package's seeds so that both sexes grow; the typical plant (sex 0.5) is female, so it shows its fruit.

generator.program.note: The cacti's own program (growth plan G2.3a): columns, barrels and chains of joints, their ribs, areoles and spines from each species' look.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy (milestone F1). Calibration against measurements and photographs comes later.
